Hi Emily—here’s a tailored Florence plan centered on Renaissance art and architecture, plus boutique historic stays that match your preferences.

Best time to go
- April–May and September–October: pleasant weather, lighter crowds than peak summer
- Book key museums 2–4 weeks ahead (longer for summer and holidays)

Core 4-day itinerary (with an optional Day 5)
Day 1: Duomo and civic heart
- Cathedral complex: Baptistery, Giotto’s Campanile, Opera del Duomo Museum; reserve Brunelleschi’s Dome climb
- Piazza della Signoria: Palazzo Vecchio (consider “Secret Passages” tour), Loggia dei Lanzi
- Orsanmichele church and its niche sculptures
- Sunset at Piazzale Michelangelo; aperitivo in San Niccolò

Day 2: Uffizi + Santa Croce/Bargello
- Uffizi Gallery (early timed entry); focus on Botticelli, Leonardo, Michelangelo, Raphael, Titian
- Santa Croce Basilica: tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo; visit the leather school (Scuola del Cuoio)
- Bargello Museum: Donatello’s David and Renaissance sculpture masterworks
- Evening stroll through the Oltrarno’s artisan workshops

Day 3: Accademia + Medici Florence
- Accademia Gallery: Michelangelo’s David (book timed slot)
- San Lorenzo complex: Medici Chapels; Basilica and Brunelleschi’s Old Sacristy
- Laurentian Library reading room (check limited opening hours)
- San Marco Museum: Fra Angelico frescoes in monastic cells

Day 4: Oltrarno treasures
- Palazzo Pitti (Palatine Gallery) and Boboli Gardens
- Brancacci Chapel (Masaccio/Masolino frescoes) at Santa Maria del Carmine—advance booking required
- Santo Spirito (Brunelleschi’s interior)
- Santa Maria Novella church and historic pharmacy (Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica)

Optional Day 5: Beyond the crowds or a short excursion
- Fiesole (15–20 min bus): Etruscan/Roman ruins, panoramic views
- Or deepen Florence: Museo dell’Opera del Duomo (if not done thoroughly), Ospedale degli Innocenti museum, Palazzo Medici Riccardi, Museo Horne, or Stibbert Museum (arms and armor)

Boutique hotels with historical character
- Antica Torre di Via Tornabuoni 1: restored medieval tower-house with rooftop terraces and river/Duomo views
- Hotel Brunelleschi: incorporates a Byzantine tower and medieval church remains; central but atmospheric
- Palazzo Niccolini al Duomo: noble residence steps from the cathedral, frescoed ceilings, period furnishings
- Relais Santa Croce by Baglioni: 18th‑century palazzo with grand salons near Santa Croce
- Palazzo Guadagni: early-16th‑century palazzo overlooking Piazza Santo Spirito; loggia terrace
- SoprArno Suites: design-forward rooms in a historic palazzo in the Oltrarno artisan quarter
- Helvetia & Bristol Firenze: late‑19th‑century grande dame with elegant, classic interiors

Hotel selection tips
- For quieter nights, consider Oltrarno (Santo Spirito/San Frediano) or streets off main squares; Duomo-area rooms can be lively
- In tower/palazzo properties, confirm elevator access and room location; request interior courtyard rooms for silence or higher floors for views
- Book cancelable rates for flexibility; popular historic boutiques fill up early

Tickets, passes, and logistics
- Timed reservations: Uffizi, Accademia, Brunelleschi’s Dome, Brancacci Chapel, and some special tours at Palazzo Vecchio
- Firenze Card (72 hours) can be cost-effective if you’re visiting many museums; some attractions still require separate time-slot bookings—check details before purchasing
- Many museums have Monday closures; verify hours on official sites
- Getting around: the historic center is walkable; avoid driving (ZTL limited-traffic zones and fines). The T2 tram links the airport to the center; taxis are reliable
- Church etiquette: shoulders covered; avoid loud conversation during services
- Crowds/pickpockets: keep valuables secure in busy areas and lines

Enrichment ideas for an art-focused trip
- Specialist Renaissance art tour or an architecture-focused walking tour (Brunelleschi, Alberti, Michelangelo)
- Evening concerts in historic churches (Santa Monaca, Santo Stefano al Ponte) or an opera night at Teatro del Maggio
- Hands-on workshop with Oltrarno artisans (bookbinding, marbled paper, gold leaf, or leather)

If you share your travel dates and budget range, I can lock in a day-by-day schedule with precise time slots and suggest room types in the hotels that fit best.
